back: The network that supports technology businesses: academic institutions, R&D centres, incubators, science parks, investors, government, industry.
Supports early-stage start-ups for a limited time with cheap workspace, mentoring, training, shared equipment and links to investors.
A site, often linked to a university, where technology and research firms locate together to share facilities and work with researchers.
Systematic work to discover new knowledge and use it to create or improve products, processes and services.
Train skilled graduates, do research, provide labs and mentors, run innovation hubs and competitions.
Turning a new idea into a product, service or process that people use and that creates value.
Incremental (small improvement), radical (completely new), disruptive (cheaper, simpler product that replaces established ones).
Empathise, define, ideate, prototype, test (repeated as needed).
Incubator: new, small start-ups, mentoring, limited time. Science park: premises for established or growing firms near research.
